23.text: The bows of the Gilyak, as may be seen from specimens in the collections

24.text: of this Museum, are strengthened with whalebone on the inside in much the

25.text: same way as the Chukchee bow. They have

26.text: a layer of sinew glued to the back, and over

27.text: that a birch-bark covering, but no backing of

28.text: plaited sinew. According to Schrenck, the

29.text: finer specimens of Gilyak bows were strength-

32.text: The two forms of bow were alike in shape:

33.text: they had recurved ends, a body flat on the

34.text: outside, and flat or rounded on the inside.

35.text: The grip was in the middle, and narrower than the arms. The bow became

36.text: thicker and narrower towards the ends, which were almost triangular in cross-

37.text: section. When unstrung, bows of both types assume a peculiar position, with

38.text: the belly slightly curved, but with horns so much turned back that sometimes

39.text: the bows look as if curved outwards.
